extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO OED staff, and disciplinary enforcement officials
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing the USPTO's reciprocal transfer of a registered practitioner to disability inactive status under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29, including notice/service, evidentiary basis, effects of transfer, and required administrative actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for reciprocal transfer (state court order / disability finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is predicated on an Order of a state Supreme Court transferring the respondent to disability inactive status for an indefinite period based on a 'Petition for Determination of Disability' and an independent medical examination report finding the respondent incapable of practicing law due to disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO may order reciprocal transfer when there is a state disciplinary disability order (here: August 16, 2017 Order of the Supreme Court, State of Colorado, Case No. 17PDJ028). Evidence cited includes the petition filed by state counsel and an independent medical examination report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice procedures (mailing and publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail to respondent's address; when the mailing was returned 'unclaimed' and 'unable to forward', the respondent was served by publication in the Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified mailing with receipt number is used if possible; if returned/unclaimed and unable to forward, service by publication in the Official Gazette is permitted and must run for two consecutive weeks. The publication must inform the respondent how to obtain copies of the Notice and Order and underlying documents by written request to the General Counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must be provided an opportunity to file, within thirty (30) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal transfer to disability inactive status based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order must set out the 30-day response period and the regulatory grounds for opposing transfer; failure to file a timely response permits the USPTO to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination standard under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d) — no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, the Office may determine that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d) and conclude that reciprocal transfer to disability inactive status is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lack of response supports a finding that no material factual dispute exists, permitting issuance of a final order transferring the practitioner to disability inactive status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of transfer — scope of practice prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is transferred to disability inactive status, precluding him from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO, until further Order of the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transfer is effective on the date of the Final Order and bars all practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and non-patent matters until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication content requirement (Official Gazette notice template)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided template, identifying the respondent, registration number, that the action is predicated on the state court order, the indefinite suspension due to disability, the prohibition on practice, and citations to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.29. It must reference availability of decisions at the OED FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template includes specific language: naming respondent and registration number; stating the underlying state order and its effect; specifying statutes/regulations relied upon; and providing the FOIA Reading Room URL for public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the transfer and the reasons for the transfer to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires affirmative notification to relevant state agencies and courts in addition to publication in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties while on disability inactive status (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while on disability inactive status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the specific duties are not recited in the order, the Final Order expressly imposes compliance with § 11.58 as a condition of disability inactive status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ('PKI') certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative action includes removing association between the practitioner and USPTO customer numbers and disabling associated PKI credentials to prevent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or using Customer Numbers until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall his name be added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bars any attempt by the respondent to obtain or be added to customer numbers during the period of disability inactive status; reinstatement is required before resuming those privileges.
